Apple___Mosaic_virus.name: Apple mosaic virus
steps: There is no cure for an infected tree; mark affected trees.
Use healthy planting material from a trusted nursery for new trees.
Wash and clean pruning tools between trees.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Leaf_spot.name: Cherry leaf spot
steps: Collect and destroy fallen leaves.
Prune to let air and sunlight into the tree.
Avoid wetting the leaves when irrigating.

Corn_(maize)___Smut.name: Maize smut
steps: Remove and destroy the swollen galls before they burst open.
Rotate away from maize for two seasons.
Use healthy seed of a tolerant variety next season.

Cotton___Bacterial_blight.name: Bacterial blight (cotton)
steps: Remove badly affected plants and destroy crop residue after picking.
Avoid overhead watering and working in the field when leaves are wet.
Use healthy seed of a tolerant variety next season.

Cotton___Herbicide_damage.name: Herbicide damage (cotton)
Cotton___Herbicide_damage.cause: weedkiller drift or residue, not a disease
steps: Check whether a weedkiller was sprayed on or near this field in the last two weeks.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress so new growth can recover.
Wash and clean the sprayer fully before using it on cotton.

Cotton___Jassid_damage.name: Jassid (leafhopper) damage
Cotton___Jassid_damage.cause: small sap-sucking insects under the leaves
steps: Look under the leaves for small green hopping insects.
Check several plants across the field before deciding how widespread it is.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.

Cotton___Leaf_curl_virus.name: Cotton leaf curl virus
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field through whiteflies.
Pull out and destroy badly affected plants early.
Remove weeds around the field that shelter whiteflies.
Use a tolerant variety next season.

Cotton___Leaf_reddening.name: Leaf reddening (cotton)
Cotton___Leaf_reddening.cause: nutrient shortage or stress, not an infection
steps: Check for waterlogging, drought or a sudden cold spell in the last weeks.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.
Ask for a soil test to find which nutrient is short.

Cotton___Leaf_variegation.name: Leaf variegation (cotton)
Cotton___Leaf_variegation.cause: usually a harmless leaf colour change
steps: Check whether only a few plants show the pattern; that is usually harmless.
Keep checking new leaves over the next week.
Take another photo if the patches grow or the leaves curl.

Grape___Downy_mildew.name: Grape downy mildew
Grape___Downy_mildew.cause: fungus-like organism; spreads fast in wet, humid weather
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a vineyard in days in humid weather.
Remove badly affected leaves and bunches.
Prune crowded shoots to improve air flow.
Avoid overhead watering.

Orange___Citrus_canker.name: Citrus canker
steps: Cut out twigs with canker spots and destroy them.
Wash and clean pruning tools between trees.
Avoid overhead watering and working among wet trees.

Peach___Leaf_curl.name: Peach leaf curl
steps: Remove and destroy curled, thickened leaves.
Keep the tree well fed and avoid water stress so it regrows healthy leaves.
Collect fallen leaves under the tree.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial leaf blight (rice)
steps: Drain the field for a few days if water is standing deep.
Do not add more nitrogen fertilizer now; it makes the blight worse.
Remove weeds and old rice stubble around the field.
Use healthy seed of a tolerant variety next season.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_streak.name: Bacterial leaf streak (rice)
steps: Do not add more nitrogen fertilizer now.
Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet.
Destroy crop residue after harvest and use healthy seed next season.

Rice___Bacterial_panicle_blight.name: Bacterial panicle blight (rice)
Rice___Bacterial_panicle_blight.cause: bacteria; worse in hot nights at flowering
steps: Check several plants across the field for upright, empty, discoloured grains.
Do not save seed from this field.
Use healthy, certified seed next season.

Rice___Blast.name: Rice blast
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field in a few humid days.
Do not add more nitrogen fertilizer now.
Keep water standing in the field; blast is worse when the soil dries.
Destroy infected crop residue after harvest.

Rice___Brown_spot.name: Brown spot (rice)
Rice___Brown_spot.cause: fungus; common on poor or dry soils
steps: Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress; brown spot marks a hungry crop.
Ask for a soil test to check potash and other nutrients.
Use healthy seed next season.

Rice___Dead_heart.name: Dead heart (stem borer)
Rice___Dead_heart.cause: stem borer caterpillars inside the stem
steps: Pull out the dried central shoots and destroy them.
Look for egg masses near the leaf tips and remove them.
Cut the stubble low and plough the residue in after harvest.

Rice___Downy_mildew.name: Downy mildew (rice)
steps: Pull out and destroy badly affected plants.
Drain water that stands too long in the nursery or field.
Use healthy seed next season.

Rice___Hispa.name: Rice hispa
Rice___Hispa.cause: small spiny beetles that scrape the leaves
steps: Look for small blue-black spiny beetles and white streaks on leaves.
Remove badly affected leaf tips and destroy them.
Remove grassy weeds on the bunds where the beetles shelter.

Rice___Tungro.name: Rice tungro
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field through leafhoppers.
Pull out and destroy badly affected plants early.
Plough in the stubble after harvest so the virus does not carry over.
Use a tolerant variety and plant at the same time as your neighbours.

Sugarcane___Mosaic.name: Sugarcane mosaic
steps: Pull out and destroy badly affected clumps.
Use healthy seed cane from a disease-free field.
Wash and clean cutting knives between fields.

Sugarcane___Red_rot.name: Red rot (sugarcane)
steps: Act quickly: it can spread across a field and ruin the cane.
Pull out and destroy infected clumps with their roots.
Do not keep a ratoon crop from this field.
Use healthy seed cane of a resistant variety and rotate the field.

Sugarcane___Rust.name: Sugarcane rust
steps: Remove badly rusted lower leaves.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.
Use a tolerant variety next planting.

Sugarcane___Yellow_leaf.name: Yellow leaf (sugarcane)
steps: Check several clumps across the field for a yellow midrib.
Use healthy seed cane from a disease-free field.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.

Tomato___Leaf_miner.name: Leaf miner (tomato)
Tomato___Leaf_miner.cause: tiny larvae tunnelling inside the leaves
steps: Remove leaves with many winding tunnels and destroy them.
Check new leaves every few days.
Remove weeds around the field.

Tomato___Nutrient_deficiency.name: Nutrient shortage (tomato)
Tomato___Nutrient_deficiency.cause: a nutrient is short in the soil, not an infection
steps: Check which leaves are yellow: old lower leaves or young top leaves.
Ask for a soil test to find which nutrient is short.
Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.

Tomato___Spotted_wilt_virus.name: Spotted wilt virus (tomato)
steps: There is no cure for infected plants; pull out and destroy them early.
Remove weeds around the field that shelter thrips.
Use healthy seedlings next season.

Wheat___Aphid.name: Aphids (wheat)
steps: Look for clusters of small green or black insects on leaves and ears.
Check several plants across the field before deciding how widespread it is.
Look for ladybird beetles; they eat aphids and often control them.

Wheat___Black_rust.name: Black (stem) rust
steps: Act quickly: rust can spread across a field and to neighbours on the wind.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today.
Use a rust-resistant variety next season.

Wheat___Blast.name: Wheat blast
steps: Act quickly: this disease can spread across a field within days.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today; this disease must be reported.
Do not save seed from this field.

Wheat___Brown_rust.name: Brown (leaf) rust
steps: Act quickly: rust can spread across a field and to neighbours on the wind.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today.
Use a rust-resistant variety next season.

Wheat___Common_root_rot.name: Common root rot (wheat)
steps: Pull out a few weak plants and look for dark brown roots and stem bases.
Rotate away from wheat and barley for a season.
Use healthy seed and avoid water stress early in the season.

Wheat___Fusarium_head_blight.name: Head blight (wheat scab)
Wheat___Fusarium_head_blight.cause: fungus; worse with rain at flowering
steps: Check the ears for bleached spikelets with pink colour at the base.
Harvest affected patches separately and do not save that grain as seed.
Plough in crop residue and rotate away from wheat and maize.

Wheat___Leaf_blight.name: Leaf blight (wheat)
steps: Keep the crop well fed and avoid water stress.
Avoid overhead watering late in the day.
Destroy infected crop residue and use healthy seed next season.

Wheat___Loose_smut.name: Loose smut (wheat)
steps: Pull out black, powdery ears carefully into a bag and destroy them.
Do not save seed from this field.
Use certified seed next season.

Wheat___Mite.name: Mites (wheat)
Wheat___Mite.cause: tiny mites; worse in dry weather
steps: Look under leaves for tiny moving dots and silvery or yellow speckling.
Avoid water stress; mites increase on a dry crop.
Check several plants across the field before deciding how widespread it is.

Wheat___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew (wheat)
steps: Check the lower leaves for white powdery patches.
Do not add more nitrogen fertilizer now; a very thick crop gets more mildew.
Use a tolerant variety and wider spacing next season.

Wheat___Septoria.name: Septoria leaf blotch (wheat)
steps: Check the lower leaves for brown blotches with tiny black dots.
Destroy infected crop residue after harvest.
Rotate away from wheat and use healthy seed next season.

Wheat___Stem_fly.name: Stem fly (wheat)
Wheat___Stem_fly.cause: maggots feeding inside the young shoot
steps: Pull out dried central shoots and look for a small maggot inside.
Check several plants across the field before deciding how widespread it is.
Sow at the recommended time next season; very early sowing gets more stem fly.

Wheat___Tan_spot.name: Tan spot (wheat)
Wheat___Tan_spot.cause: fungus that survives on old wheat straw
steps: Check leaves for tan spots with a yellow ring.
Plough in or remove old wheat residue.
Rotate away from wheat for a season.

Wheat___Yellow_rust.name: Yellow (stripe) rust
steps: Act quickly: rust can spread across a field and to neighbours on the wind.
Contact your agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre today.
Use a rust-resistant variety next season.
